solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exams even grasped by idiot

indicators.note: something grasped by another is held inside it, so the word for idiot wraps round the other piece

parts.note: an ass is a fool
level means flat or even

explanation.surface: A student's exams are being sat by a fool, who holds them all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: AS LEVELS are British school exams taken around age 17, a step below A levels.
explanation.definitionFit: AS levels are a kind of British school examination, so they are exams.

clue.text: Sketch given out by circulation of English Times

indicators.note: out can mean disordered, so the letters of given are jumbled
circulation suggests moving round, so the letters of the next pieces are stirred about

parts.note: T is short for time, so two of them stand for times

explanation.surface: A short piece handed out to readers via the circulation of a newspaper, The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is just two Ts. 'out' rearranges GIVEN to VIGNE; 'circulation of' turns E and TT into TTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a short descriptive piece of writing or a brief scene, i.e. a sketch.

clue.text: Melee over party following vacation drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: a scrum is a disorderly crowd or scuffle

indicators.note: vacation means emptying out, so the inside of party is removed leaving its ends

explanation.surface: After a holiday rush, a party crowd gets a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday but means emptying: party emptied of its middle letters gives PY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is rough strong cider from the West Country of England, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: One whose aims are hidden

parts.note: aims reads as secret intentions but means the gun is pointed from a concealed position

explanation.surface: Someone with a secret agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aims' suggests hidden motives; literally it is a marksman taking aim from cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper shoots from a concealed spot, so whoever does the aiming is out of sight.

clue.text: Formal stretch test

parts.note: dry can mean stiff, impersonal and formal in manner
a run is a continuous stretch, as in a run of good luck

explanation.surface: A formal period of time trialling something.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a rehearsal or trial before the real thing, so a test.

clue.text: Whenever following service, principal creates high ground

indicators.note: following places the word for whenever after the church service

parts.note: Mass is a church service
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains I stay in'
central means chief or principal

explanation.surface: After church, the head teacher makes a climb up the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The MASSIF CENTRAL is the highland region of south-central France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massif Central is a large upland plateau in France, an area of high ground.

clue.text: Sort of service blow-outs where tyres are fitted

parts.note: a blow-out is a large feast, so blow-outs are big meals
tyres go on the rims of a vehicle's road wheels

explanation.surface: A garage service dealing with punctures and fitting new tyres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow-outs' and 'tyres' suggest burst tyres; here blow-outs are slap-up meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals on wheels is a delivery service bringing hot food to elderly or housebound people.

clue.text: Zero oil initially used up, acquiring thrust in continental style

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so the jumbled letters enclose the word for thrust
up can mean in disorder or astir, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a squat thrust is a gym exercise, so squat is paired with thrust

explanation.surface: Engine oil running out at zero, with a push forward in European fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals the anagram and 'acquiring' the container; thrust gives SQUAT via the gym exercise, the squat thrust. The style is the ornate French fashion of Louis XIV's reign.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Quatorze names the grand French decorative style of the era of Louis XIV, a continental style.

clue.text: Beware to get sent back near swinging club?

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, old school slang for a lookout's warning

indicators.note: sent back means the letters for near are written backwards

explanation.surface: A warning that one is about to be sent back near a club swung around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging club' suggests a golf club; it is the Cavern Club in Liverpool, the famous 1960s venue where the Beatles played.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cavern was a famous Swinging Sixties nightclub in Liverpool, hence a club of that era.

clue.text: Drinker shouldn't begin to dilute punch

indicators.note: should not begin tells us the word's opening letter is dropped, read as S not beginning it

parts.note: a supper is one who sups, i.e. a drinker
to cut a drink is to water it down

explanation.surface: A drinker advised not to start watering down the punch bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punch' looks like the drink but is the blow. 'shouldn't begin' removes S, a play on 'shouldn't', from SUPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is an upward punch in boxing, a blow to the chin.

clue.text: Sort of wooden 'ead-gear

definitions.meaning: describes things made from a particular hardwood timber, as in a chair of that wood
head-gear with the H dropped Cockney style: a helm, or helmet, loses its aitch too

explanation.surface: A wooden helmet, pronounced with a dropped aitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ead' signals a dropped H, so helm (an old word for helmet) is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree's timber names its furniture, as in an elm table, and a helm minus its aitch is head-gear.

clue.text: Emerging topless promotion …

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, that is its first letter

parts.note: nascent means just coming into being

explanation.surface: Someone appearing without a top earns an advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a rise, so a promotion is an ascent up the ranks.

clue.text: … presents false front?

definitions.note: front in the sense of brazen cheek or impudence, a noun

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are rearranged into a different word

explanation.surface: Continuing from the last clue: an emerging topless figure presents a false front.
explanation.definitionFit: Front can mean cheeky boldness, and pertness is sauciness or cheek.

clue.text: Reportedly puts pleats in formal dress

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to tuck fabric is to fold it into pleats, so puts pleats in gives tucks

explanation.surface: A tailor reportedly pleats a formal suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tux is short for tuxedo, a dinner jacket worn as formal evening wear.

clue.text: Middle Eastern diet that contributes to sickness, etc

indicators.note: contributes to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern diet that causes sickness and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition swept in 'that', which is a link word joining definition to wordplay. 'diet' suggests food; it is a legislative assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Knesset is Israel's parliament, and a diet is a formal legislative assembly.

clue.text: Runner that could be on the tail of a Russian athlete?

definitions.text: Runner that could be on the tail of a Russian athlete?

parts.words: Runner that could be on the tail of a Russian athlete?
parts.note: runner here is a sled blade, and many Russian surnames end in these three letters

explanation.surface: A runner chasing a Russian rival close behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A ski is a runner on snow; many Russian surnames, such as an athlete's, end in -ski.
explanation.definitionFit: Skis are long runners for gliding on snow, and the ending appears at the tail of many Russian names.

clue.text: Saying about foreign character's top degree

parts.note: a maxim is a proverb or saying

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the Greek letter is written backwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A proverb about a foreigner's highest academic qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: Maximum means the highest possible amount or extent, the top degree of something.

clue.text: Somewhere in the East, friend dons a short garment

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the friend gets covered by the clothing pieces
short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a habit is a monk's or nun's robe
bud is American slang for a pal

explanation.surface: Out East, a friend puts on a cropped garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the capital of the United Arab Emirates, a place in the Middle East.

clue.text: Lewdly, I see, pinching wobbly rump

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing hold of, so the outer pieces hold the jumbled letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat or see of a bishop

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lecherous confession: I see, while pinching a jiggling bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb; it is a bishop's district, and Ely is an English cathedral city. 'wobbly' signals the anagram and 'pinching' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Impurely means in an unchaste or indecent way, which is how lewdly behaves.

clue.text: Judge in Ulster undermines vile dog

indicators.note: in a down clue, undermines puts the following piece underneath the one for vile

parts.note: base means low and contemptible

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for judge within the one for Ulster

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish judge subverts a nasty dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a barkless hunting breed from central Africa, a type of dog.

clue.text: One succeeded old lady after daily appeal

indicators.note: after places the remaining pieces behind the word for daily

parts.note: a daily or char is a cleaning woman who comes in each day
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
ma is a familiar word for mother, one's old lady

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded their mother following a newspaper appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like a newspaper; it is a char, the British term for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal magnetism or allure, i.e. appeal.

clue.text: Enigma of king having useless duke taken in

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the duke's letter sits within the word for useless

parts.note: idle can mean futile or pointless, as in idle threats

explanation.surface: The mystery of a king who has taken in a lazy duke.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question or mystery, an enigma.

clue.text: Snack, for example, drinker regularly scoffed

indicators.note: scoffed means eaten up, so the alternate letters go inside

parts.note: say introduces an example, as in 'a fruit, say, an apple'

indicators.note: regularly picks letters at even intervals from the word

explanation.surface: A snack, for instance, wolfed down by a regular drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: SARNEY is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarnie or sarney is informal British for a sandwich, a common snack.

clue.text: Ruth by lift that's difficult to control

parts.note: to lift something is to raise it up
ruth is an old word for compassion or pity

explanation.surface: A woman called Ruth in an elevator who is hard to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a name; it is the archaic word for pity, as in ruthless. 'by' sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity means arrogant and self-important, not inclined to obey, hence hard to keep in line.

clue.text: Polish knight has gone blue

indicators.note: has gone means the knight's letter is missing from the word

parts.note: to sand is to smooth or polish a surface
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A Polish knight has died and turned melancholy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the verb to polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means down or melancholy, a synonym for sad.

clue.text: Lady digesting first of reports on low-down officer

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the lady part follows the information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the low-down

indicators.note: digesting means swallowing, so the lady holds the letter inside

parts.note: a dame is a lady, also a titled woman

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A woman absorbing the first reports on the inside story about a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French police officer.

clue.text: Artist has to run around city

indicators.note: around means the word for run encloses the artist

parts.note: to hare is to run fast
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter has to dash round town.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital city of Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Time to celebrate live blues, half rejigged for broadcasting

indicators.note: broadcasting means scattering widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: half takes the first half of the word's letters

explanation.surface: Live blues music, partly reworked to go out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes REJI from rejigged; 'for broadcasting' scatters it with LIVE BLUES.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver jubilee is the 25th anniversary, an occasion for celebration.
